theory.overview: Linked lists are fundamental data structures consisting of nodes, each containing data and a reference (pointer) to the next node. Unlike arrays, linked lists don't require contiguous memory allocation—nodes can be scattered anywhere in memory, connected by pointers. This flexibility enables efficient insertion and deletion at any position ($O(1)$ if you have the pointer to the node), but comes with trade-offs: random access is $O(n)$ (must traverse from head), and memory overhead is higher due to pointer storage. Understanding linked lists is crucial for implementing other structures like stacks, queues, and graphs, and they appear frequently in interview questions involving operations on sequences.

sections.title: Singly Linked List Structure
sections.content: A singly linked list consists of nodes with two fields: data and next (pointer to next node). The list is accessed via a head pointer. The last node's next points to null. Basic operations: insert at head ($O(1)$), insert after given node ($O(1)$), delete from head ($O(1)$), delete after given node ($O(1)$), search ($O(n)$). The key insight: with a pointer to a node, you can insert/delete after it in constant time, but you can't easily insert before without a pointer to the previous node.

sections.title: Doubly Linked List
sections.content: Doubly linked lists have nodes with three fields: data, next, and prev (pointer to previous node). This enables bidirectional traversal and $O(1)$ deletion of a node when you have its pointer (no need for previous pointer). Trade-off: more memory (extra pointer per node) and slightly more complex insertion/deletion (must update two pointers). Used in implementing LRU cache, undo/redo functionality, and when bidirectional traversal is needed.

sections.title: Circular Linked List
sections.content: In a circular linked list, the last node's next points back to the head instead of null. This enables continuous traversal—useful for round-robin scheduling, implementing queues with circular buffers, and problems where you need to cycle through elements. Circular singly linked lists require care to detect when you've traversed the entire list (check if current.next == head). Circular doubly linked lists are common (DLL with head.prev = tail and tail.next = head).

sections.title: Linked List vs Array
sections.content: Arrays excel at random access ($O(1)$) and have excellent cache locality (contiguous memory). They're memory-efficient (no pointers). Linked lists excel at insertion/deletion ($O(1)$ with pointer) and don't require resizing. They use memory efficiently for dynamic growth (allocate nodes as needed). Arrays suffer from $O(n)$ insertion/deletion (shifting required) and fixed capacity (without resizing). Linked lists suffer from $O(n)$ access, poor cache locality, and pointer overhead. Choose based on operation patterns: arrays for access-heavy, linked lists for modification-heavy.

sections.title: Common Linked List Techniques
sections.content: Fast and slow pointers (tortoise and hare): one pointer moves 1 step, another moves 2 steps. Used to find middle of list ($O(n)$), detect cycles ($O(n)$), find cycle start, find $k$-th from end. Dummy head technique: create a dummy node before head to simplify edge cases (deleting head, inserting before head). Runner technique: advance one pointer $k$ steps, then move both together to find $k$-th from end. Reversal: iterative (three pointers) or recursive (reverse rest, link current to previous).

techniques.name: Runner

keyConcepts.name: Pointer Manipulation
keyConcepts.description: Core linked list operations involve updating next pointers. Always draw diagrams to verify pointer updates. Common bug: losing reference to remaining list when reassigning.
keyConcepts.tip: Save next before reassigning: next = node.next; node.next = newNode; newNode.next = next

keyConcepts.name: Sentinel/Dummy Node
keyConcepts.description: Dummy node before head eliminates special cases for head operations. All operations become uniform: work on dummy.next instead of head.
keyConcepts.benefit: Simpler code, fewer edge cases to check

keyConcepts.name: Memory Management
keyConcepts.description: In languages without GC (C), must free deleted nodes to prevent leaks. In managed languages, dereference nodes so GC can reclaim. Watch for cycles preventing GC.
keyConcepts.critical: Always update pointers when deleting to avoid memory leaks

keyConcepts.name: Cycle Detection
keyConcepts.description: Floyd's cycle detection: fast pointer moves 2 steps, slow moves 1. If they meet, cycle exists. To find start: reset one to head, move both at 1 step until they meet.
keyConcepts.proof: Distance from head to cycle start = distance from meeting point to cycle start mod cycle length

steps.title: Create Node
steps.description: Allocate new node with data. Set next to null initially.
steps.code: Node newNode = new Node(data); newNode.next = null;

steps.title: Link to List
steps.description: Set newNode.next to current head, then update head to newNode.

steps.title: Traverse
steps.description: Start from head, follow next pointers until null.
steps.code: Node current = head; while (current != null) current = current.next;

steps.title: Delete Node
steps.description: To delete after given node: set node.next = node.next.next.

steps.title: Memory Cleanup
steps.description: In languages without GC, free deleted node. In GC languages, just dereference.
steps.code: Node deleted = node.next; node.next = deleted.next; deleted = null;

practiceProblems.title: Reverse Linked List
practiceProblems.description: Reverse a singly linked list.
practiceProblems.solution: Iterative: three pointers (prev, curr, next). For each node, reverse its next to point to prev, advance all three. Return prev. Recursive: reverse rest, link current to previous.
hints: Need three pointers: prev, current, next

practiceProblems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
practiceProblems.description: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
practiceProblems.solution: Dummy head technique. Compare heads of both lists, append smaller to result, advance that list. When one list exhausted, append remaining of other.
hints: Append remaining when one list ends

practiceProblems.title: Linked List Cycle
practiceProblems.description: Detect if a linked list has a cycle.
practiceProblems.solution: Floyd's cycle detection. Fast pointer (2 steps), slow pointer (1 step). If they meet, cycle exists. If fast reaches null, no cycle.
hints: Two pointers: fast (2 steps), slow (1 step)
If fast reaches null, no cycle

practiceProblems.title: Middle of Linked List
practiceProblems.description: Find the middle node of a linked list. If even length, return second middle.
practiceProblems.solution: Fast/slow pointers. Fast moves 2 steps, slow moves 1. When fast reaches end, slow is at middle.
hints: When fast at end, slow at middle

practiceProblems.title: Remove Nth Node From End
practiceProblems.description: Remove the nth node from the end of linked list.
practiceProblems.solution: Two passes: find length, then traverse to length-n. Or one pass: advance runner n steps, then move both until runner at end. Delete node after slow.
hints: Runner technique: advance n steps first
Then move both until runner at end

practiceProblems.title: Reorder List
practiceProblems.description: Reorder list: L0→Ln→L1→Ln-1→L2→Ln-2...
practiceProblems.solution: Find middle, reverse second half, then merge two halves alternately.
hints: Merge alternately: first from first half, then from second

practiceProblems.title: Palindrome Linked List
practiceProblems.description: Check if linked list is a palindrome.
practiceProblems.solution: Find middle with fast/slow. Reverse second half. Compare first half with reversed second half. Restore list if needed (reverse second half again).
hints: Compare first half with reversed second half

practiceProblems.title: Intersection of Two Linked Lists
practiceProblems.description: Find the node where two linked lists intersect.
practiceProblems.solution: Get lengths of both lists. Advance longer list by difference. Then move both pointers together until they meet (intersection) or both reach null (no intersection).
hints: Move both together until they match

practiceProblems.title: Sort List
practiceProblems.description: Sort linked list using merge sort.
practiceProblems.solution: Find middle with slow/fast. Recursively sort both halves. Merge sorted halves. Base case: empty or single node.

practiceProblems.title: Rotate List
practiceProblems.description: Rotate list to the right by k places.
practiceProblems.solution: Find length, connect tail to head (make circular). Find new tail at position (length - k % length). New head is new tail.next. Break circular link.
hints: Find new tail: length - k positions from head
New head = new tail.next, break circular link

practiceProblems.title: Add Two Numbers
practiceProblems.description: Add two numbers represented as reversed linked lists (digits in nodes).
practiceProblems.solution: Traverse both lists simultaneously, add digits with carry. Create new node for sum digit. Continue until both lists exhausted and carry is 0.
hints: Add digits with carry from previous
Create new node for each digit, handle carry at end

practiceProblems.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
practiceProblems.description: Copy a linked list where each node has a random pointer to any node or null.
practiceProblems.solution: First pass: create copy nodes, insert after original. Second pass: set copy.random = original.random.next. Third pass: separate original and copy lists.

practiceProblems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List
practiceProblems.description: Remove duplicates from sorted linked list.
practiceProblems.solution: Traverse list. If current.val == current.next.val, set current.next = current.next.next (skip duplicate). Else advance current.

practiceProblems.title: Remove All Duplicates
practiceProblems.description: Remove all nodes with duplicate values from sorted list (keep only distinct).
practiceProblems.solution: Dummy head. Compare current.next with current.next.next. If duplicate, skip all duplicates (advance while same value). Else advance current.
hints: Use dummy head to handle head deletion
Only keep first of each unique value

practiceProblems.title: Swap Nodes in Pairs
practiceProblems.description: Swap every two adjacent nodes in linked list.
practiceProblems.solution: Iterative with dummy head. For each pair: first.next = second.next, second.next = first, prev.next = second. Move pointers appropriately.
hints: Update previous pointer to link swapped pair

practiceProblems.title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
practiceProblems.description: Reverse nodes of linked list in groups of k. If fewer than k remain, leave as is.
practiceProblems.solution: Count k nodes. If k nodes exist, reverse them. Recursively process remaining list. Link reversed group to result of recursion.
hints: Check if k nodes exist before reversing
Reverse k nodes, link to rest

practiceProblems.title: Detect Cycle Start
practiceProblems.description: Find the node where cycle begins in linked list.
practiceProblems.solution: Detect cycle with fast/slow. When they meet, reset one to head. Move both at 1 step. Where they meet is cycle start.
hints: When they meet, reset one to head
Move both at 1 step - meeting point is start

practiceProblems.title: Flatten Multilevel Doubly Linked List
practiceProblems.description: Flatten a doubly linked list where each node has child pointer (can be null or another list).
practiceProblems.solution: Traverse list. When child exists, save next, flatten child recursively, link current to child head, child tail to saved next.
hints: When child found, flatten it first

practiceProblems.title: LRU Cache with Linked List
practiceProblems.description: Implement LRU cache using doubly linked list + hash map.
practiceProblems.solution: Hash map maps key to node. DLL maintains access order (MRU at head, LRU at tail). On get: move to head. On put: update or add to head, evict LRU if over capacity.
hints: MRU at head, LRU at tail

practiceProblems.title: Add Two Numbers II
practiceProblems.description: Add two numbers represented as linked lists (not reversed).
practiceProblems.solution: Reverse both lists, add, reverse result. Or use stacks: push all digits, pop and add with carry, build result.
hints: Or use stacks to reverse order

practiceProblems.title: Odd Even Linked List
practiceProblems.description: Group all odd-indexed nodes together followed by even-indexed nodes.
practiceProblems.solution: Separate into odd and even lists. Traverse original, append to odd or even based on index. Link odd tail to even head.
hints: Link odd tail to even head

practiceProblems.title: Split Linked List in Parts
practiceProblems.description: Split linked list into k consecutive parts with尽可能 equal size.
practiceProblems.solution: Calculate base size = n/k, extra = n % k. First 'extra' parts have size base+1, rest have size base. Traverse and split accordingly.
hints: Base size = n/k, extra = n % k
First 'extra' parts get one extra node
Traverse and split at calculated sizes

practiceProblems.title: Design Linked List
practiceProblems.description: Design singly linked list with get, addAtHead, addAtTail, addAtIndex, deleteAtIndex.
practiceProblems.solution: Maintain head and size. For index operations, traverse to position. Handle edge cases (empty list, invalid index).
hints: Traverse to index for indexed operations

practiceProblems.title: Next Greater Node Value
practiceProblems.description: For each node, find next node with greater value. Store in array.
practiceProblems.solution: Reverse list. Use stack to track nodes. For each node, pop while stack top's value ≤ current. Result for popped nodes is current. Push current.
hints: Reverse list to process from right to left
When popping, that node's answer is current

practiceProblems.title: Insertion Sort List
practiceProblems.description: Sort linked list using insertion sort.
practiceProblems.solution: Maintain sorted portion (initially head). For each unsorted node, find its position in sorted portion, insert. Continue until all sorted.
hints: For each unsorted node, find position in sorted

snippets.title: Node Definition
Reverse Iterative
snippets.code:
def reverse_list(head):
    prev = None
    curr = head
    while curr:
        next_temp = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = next_temp
    return prev  # O(n) time, O(1) space
